result:
I'd dissolve the gap between how people actually experience the world and what they believe about each other across divides.

Not through forced agreement. But that moment when someone realizes the person they've written off as simply evil or stupid is actually reasoning from different premises, or has seen different evidence, or values something they hadn't considered—and that this doesn't require abandoning their own convictions.

Most of the worst things seem to compound because people can't quite imagine the internal logic of those who disagree. We're stuck narrating each other as characters in our own stories rather than as people navigating something genuinely complicated.

That shift—which is small and happens locally all the time—at scale might actually matter.
